reason: Plan critic returned revise on both rounds; one high-severity issue stands. BLOCKING: plan requirements 1 and 3 (accepts only a demonstrably interrupted IMPLEMENTING task; fail closed when the interruption cannot be established) have no acceptance criterion that exercises refusal. AC-1 covers only the eligible path and AC-3 covers only the lock override, so recover could be implemented as an unconditional status setter - accepting a task in any state, one with a terminating event, or one already carrying CLAUDE_FIX_STARTED - and all 16 verify commands would still pass. That is exactly the hand-edit defect the verb exists to remove. Also unresolved: nothing asserts the interrupted work on disk survives recovery, so a recovery that reset files would pass; AC-9 does not settle that the rounds-exhausted blocking critique specifically is persisted, nor its round/plan-version identity; AC-16 rests on a baseline test count the implementer itself picks, so a low literal satisfies it; AC-12 needs a hand-rolled ci.yml reader under stdlib-only and must fail rather than skip when the file is missing or unparsable; all 16 criteria are unittest tests the implementer authors and none drives orchestrator.py as a subprocess through real CLI dispatch; CLAUDE.md is not declared, so its verb list and its IMPLEMENTING-has-one-exit narrative will contradict the code; and _support.py is declared while its fixture work could be written inline, risking a declared-but-unchanged validation failure. requirement.md has been extended with criteria 14-18 and three new constraints covering all of the above - read it before replanning. KEEP from v1: the file set is right, including .ai/hooks/session_start.py, .ai/hooks/stop_guard.py and .ai/hooks/pre_tool_use.py, and AC-14 and AC-15 correctly single-home the blackboard and make the guard read the authoritative approved plan.

Plan critic passed v2, but five substantive non-blocking issues stand and two of them are not polish. (1) AC-3 weakens a fail-closed guarantee in translation: the requirement says a recovered task cannot reach VALIDATED without validation having run, while AC-3 only asserts recovery emits no validation or completion event. Not emitting an event during recover does not settle that the route afterwards still requires validation. (2) The plan calls the persisted critique artifact orchestrator-owned evidence, but PROTECTED_EVIDENCE_PATTERNS in .ai/hooks/pre_tool_use.py lists only state.json, events.jsonl, baseline.json, test-results.json, validation.md and review-findings.json. As planned this ships a new evidence file a worker can write its own version of, which contradicts the rule that no plan can authorise a worker to write its own verdict. Both pre_tool_use.py and CLAUDE.md are already declared, so this needs no change to the file set. (3) Requirement criterion 8 is half covered: nothing asserts worker and acceptance subprocess launching falls back to the orchestrator checkout when state.worktree is null, and TASK-008 own state.json has worktree null, so this is the path this very task runs on. (4) AC-3 bundles lock refusal, override attribution and no-manufactured-completion into one implementer-authored test method; unbundle them. (5) AC-18 never states where the critique artifact lives or how it is named, so a developer told to read it at the gate cannot find it and a reviewer cannot tell a stale round from the current one. Additionally, F2 residual case must be written into the plan risks: structural ownership leaves a concurrent task with no recorded worktree editing shared source still producing blocking violations in task A. That narrowing follows from decision 2 and is accepted, but it must be accepted knowingly. requirement.md now carries criteria 19-23 covering all of the above. KEEP v2 wholesale otherwise: the 14-file set is right, and AC-14/15/16 refusal paths, AC-17 byte preservation, AC-19 real CLI subprocess dispatch, AC-20 CLAUDE.md verb-contract parsing and AC-12 fail-not-skip are all correct and must be retained.

Plan v3 passed the critic, but four of its five remaining issues are closed by developer decision rather than accepted. (1) AC-3 carries two claims and its command settles one: the statement says lock refusal happens without using a PID liveness probe as authorization, but test_existing_lock_refuses_without_override only tests refusal in general, so an implementation that probes os.kill(pid,0) and proceeds when the pid looks dead would satisfy the command while violating decision 4. Add an explicit dead-PID test proving PID liveness cannot authorize recovery; pid data may be advisory detail in the event only. (2) Constraint 3 keeps recovery metadata out of state.json because task-state.schema.json sets additionalProperties false, but no criterion enforces it - validate the post-recovery state.json against that schema and assert it passes. (3) The declared file list can strand the implementer. Rooting subprocesses at the recorded worktree most plausibly changes worker_env, and test_preflight.py (which calls orch.worker_env for a task with no state or worktree), test_worktree_pr.py, test_validation_profile.py and test_review_package.py all exercise that or cwd/merge-base behaviour while undeclared. AC-16 requires the whole suite to pass, so a behaviour change breaking any of them leaves the implementer unable to fix it (undeclared write, denied at the tool boundary) and unable to leave it (criterion fails). Re-evaluate and correct the file list: preferably design the change to be backward compatible and state in the plan why each module is unaffected, otherwise declare only those that genuinely must change, remembering a declared file left byte-identical fails as declared-but-unchanged. Do not leave a path where AC-16 fails while the implementer is forbidden to fix the failing test. (5) Make hook resolution authoritative and testable. .claude/settings.json registers hooks as cwd-relative commands, so once worker cwd is the recorded worktree the scripts that execute are that worktree copies, not the orchestrator checkout copies. Decide explicitly which copy is authoritative, state it in the plan, and add a criterion proving the intended copy ran - AC-27 and AC-28 currently pass either way, so neither settles it. Issue 4 (the ADR for worktree-rooted execution with single-homed evidence) may remain a documented non-blocking risk; write it only if it falls out naturally, do not expand scope. requirement.md now carries criteria 24-27 covering all of the above. KEEP v3 otherwise in full: objective, the 15 requirements, all 28 existing criteria, constraints 1-18 including constraint 17 about extending fd35909 rather than re-deriving it, and risks 4, 7 and 10.
